status_summary: A USDA Food and Nutrition Service memo dated 2025-07-07, Guidance on the Interpretation of Discrimination Based on Sex in USDA Child Nutrition Programs, rescinds the May 2022 Bostock policy update and its related documents, cites Executive Order 14168, applies the 2020 Title IX rule and USDA's longstanding Title IX regulations, and ends pending compliance reviews based on the 2022 policy. The memo follows a 2025-07-02 settlement in which the Justice Department, for USDA, agreed to the rescission in exchange for dismissal of a Louisiana school board's lawsuit; the joint stipulation filed that day dismisses only the count against USDA and its Secretary, and the school board's claims against the Department of Health and Human Services and other federal defendants were still being litigated in a filing dated 2026-07-23. No statute or government-wide rule barring all agencies from such withholding in the future was found. Separately, USDA froze some funds to Maine on 2025-04-02 in a dispute over the state's policy on transgender students in sports; a temporary restraining order in April and a court-approved settlement on 2025-05-02 ended the freeze. That episode involved a state with a gender-identity-inclusive policy and falls outside what this recommendation addresses.

timeline.event: USDA announced a freeze of some federal funds to Maine over the state's policy on transgender students in sports; a temporary restraining order in April 2025 barred the freeze pending further proceedings.
USDA and Maine reached a court-approved settlement under which USDA funds to the state may not be frozen.

The Justice Department, on USDA's behalf, executed a settlement with the Rapides Parish School Board dismissing its lawsuit against the 2022 policy in exchange for USDA rescinding it, as described in the USDA memo.

The FNS Administrator issued a memo rescinding the May 2022 Bostock policy update, its Q and A and cover letter, adopting a male-or-female reading of sex in child nutrition programs and ending pending compliance reviews based on the 2022 policy.

Civil Eats reports that the USDA guidance posted 2025-07-07 for state school meal administrators rescinded, effective immediately, the earlier requirement to prohibit discrimination based on gender identity and sexual orientation in federal meal programs, citing litigation risk.

title: Bar agencies from withholding school meal funds over SOGI readings of Title IX
uncertainties: The USDA memo was read in full on usda.gov; it has no memo code. The FNS guidance page shows a last-updated date of 2026-02-20, which may reflect later edits and is not used as an event. Executive Order 14168 is cited in the memo and is covered in c11-06; its directive to agencies to rescind inconsistent guidance is a government-wide policy but not a specific bar on funding withholding. The outcome of the 22-state attorneys general lawsuit filed in 2022 and the 2022 House bill were not checked. The Maine episode concerns athletics policy rather than the Mandate's SOGI reading of Title IX and is listed for context only; the TRO date was not stated in the source. Whether other agencies (HHS, DOJ) retain comparable policies was not checked. Freshness check of 2026-10-19: no later USDA memo, proposed or final rule, statute or court order concerning the 2025-07-07 rescission was found; the USDA guidance page still carries only the title and a link to the memo (updated 2026-02-20). A Federal Register API search for Bostock and school nutrition since 2025-07-01 returned two unrelated documents (an HHS Medicaid rule and a proposed government-wide federal financial assistance rule, 2026-05-29); the latter was not read and its bearing on school meal funds is unknown. H.R. 8781, the Title IX Clarification Act of 2026, was reported by the House Committee on Education and Workforce on 2026-09-08 (H. Rept. 119-798); its govinfo record does not mention school meals or withholding of funds and the bill text was not read, so it is not counted as the recommended bar on withholding; a Senate bill of the same name noted by the researcher was not checked in review. The Supreme Court decision in West Virginia v. B.P.J. (2026-06-30) is cited in the 2026-07-23 Rapides Parish filing; it is a sports case and was not read here. No appropriations provision barring withholding of school meal funds was located.
